questions.q_en:
Parts of a sentence are given below in jumbled order. Select the option that arranges the parts in the correct sequence to form a meaningful sentence.

(P) to solve complex problems

(Q) quantum computing promises

(O) currently intractable for even

(R) the most powerful classical supercomputers
questions.solution_en:
The sentence most logically starts with part (Q) "Quantum computing promises", which introduces the subject ("Quantum computing") and the main verb ("promises"). This sets up the expectation of what it promises.

Part (P) "to solve complex problems" is an infinitive phrase that acts as the object of the verb "promises," detailing what quantum computing aims to achieve. So far: "Quantum computing promises to solve complex problems".

Part (O) "currently intractable for even" is an adjectival phrase that modifies "complex problems," describing their nature. The word "even" suggests a comparison or an extreme will follow.

Part (R) "the most powerful classical supercomputers." completes the adjectival phrase started in (O), providing the object of "for" and specifying what these problems are intractable for.

Thus, the correct and meaningful order of the sentence is QPOR.

The sentence formed after rearrangement is: Quantum computing promises to solve complex problems currently intractable for even the most powerful classical supercomputers.

Hence, the correct answer is option (b).

Parts of a sentence are given below in jumbled order. Select the option that arranges the parts in the correct sequence to form a meaningful sentence.

(P) improve resource management,

(Q) and promote sustainable urban development

(O) to enhance citizen services,

(R) smart cities integrate technology
questions.solution_en:
The sentence naturally starts with part (R) "Smart cities integrate technology", which forms the main subject ("Smart cities") and verb ("integrate") along with its object ("technology"). This establishes the core action.

Part (O) "to enhance citizen services," is an infinitive phrase of purpose, explaining why smart cities integrate technology, listing the first objective. So far: "Smart cities integrate technology to enhance citizen services,".

Part (P) "improve resource management," lists a second objective, parallel to (O). The "to" from "to enhance" is implied before "improve." It continues the list of purposes.

Part (Q) "and promote sustainable urban development" provides the third and final objective in the series, connected by the conjunction "and."

Thus, the correct and meaningful order of the sentence is ROPQ.

The sentence formed after rearrangement is: Smart cities integrate technology to enhance citizen services, improve resource management, and promote sustainable urban development.

Hence, the correct answer is option (d).

questions.q_en:
Select the option that expresses the given sentence in reported speech.

Raghav said to Meera, "Are you upset with me?"
options_en: Raghav asked Meera if she was upset with her.
Raghav asked Meera if she was upset with him.
Raghav asked Meera if she was upset with me.
Raghav asked Meera why she was upset with him.
questions.solution_en:
In the case of Interrogative sentences like this, "said" in Direct Speech is changed into "enquired (of)", "wanted to know", "asked", etc.

In Indirect speech, the verb is always placed after the subject, unlike in Direct Speech.

If there is a question in the Direct Speech whose answer can come as "Yes" or "No" in the Indirect Speech, we should use the conjunctions "if" or "whether".

For example:

Ravi said to me, "Is she studying?" (Direct Speech)

Ravi asked me if she was studying. (Indirect Speech)

Also, the sentence in the Direct Speech is in the Simple Present tense. So, the tense in the Indirect Speech should be in the Simple Past tense.

The following things in the sentence should change when changed from Direct speech to Indirect Speech:

'If' would be introduced in the sentence.

The pronouns 'you' and 'me' would be changed to 'she' and 'him' respectively.

'Are you' would be changed to 'she was'.

Therefore, the correct answer is option (b): Raghav asked Meera if she was upset with him.

questions.q_en:
Select the option that expresses the given sentence in direct speech.

Ned Stark said that he had to go to Kings Landing then.
options_en: Ned Stark said, "I must go to Kings Landing then."
Ned Stark said, "I had to go to Kings Landing now."
Ned Stark said, "I must be gone to the Kings Landing now."
Ned Stark said, "I must go to Kings Landing now."
questions.solution_en:
The correct answer is (d) Ned Stark said, "I must go to Kings Landing now."

Key points:

• When "must" denotes morality or universality, there isn't any change in the use of "must".

• For example:

o The Professor said that we must love our country. (Indirect Speech)

o The Professor said, "We must love our country." (Direct Speech)

• However, if the use of "must" doesn't denote universality or morality, then the tense form changes as per the normal rules. "Had to" in Indirect Speech is changed into "must" in Direct Speech. (The question is in reference to this rule.)

• For example:

o Rahul said that he had to go to school at once. (Indirect Speech)

o Rahul said, "I must go to school at once." (Direct Speech)

• The following things in the sentence will change when changed from Indirect Speech to Direct Speech:

thennow

• Therefore, the correct answer is: Ned Stark said, "I must go to Kings Landing now."

Select the most appropriate homophones to fill the blanks.

She had to ___________ the ___________ to stop the water from leaking.
questions.solution_en:
"Seal" is the verb that means to close off or block something to prevent the passage of air or water. "Ceiling" refers to the overhead surface that covers the top of a room. The complete sentence is "She had to seal the ceiling to stop the water from leaking."

questions.q_en:
Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence.

No sooner had she finished her breakfast that she had received a phone call from her boss, informing her that she needed to come to work immediately.
questions.solution_en:
The structure "no sooner" is followed by "than" in standard English to indicate two events happening in quick succession. The underlined segment, "that she had received," is incorrect because "that" should be "than," and the verb tense should be past simple ("received") to match the sequence of events in the past, as "had finished" is past perfect, indicating the first action.

Option a, "than she receives," uses present tense, which is incorrect for a past event.

Option b, "than she received," corrects "that" to "than" and uses the correct past tense.

Option c, "that she receives," retains "that" and uses incorrect present tense.

Option d, "that she received," retains the incorrect "that."

Hence, the correct answer is option (b).

questions.q_en:
A sentence has been given in Active/Passive Voice. Out of the four alternatives suggested, select the one which best expresses the same sentence in Passive/Active Voice.

Bring a glass of water.
options_en: Let a glass of water be brought.
Let a glass of water is brought.
Let a glass of water has to be brought.
Let a glass of water is to be brought.
questions.solution_en:
The subject of the Active Voice is changed into the object of the Passive Voice. Also, the object of the Active Voice is changed into the subject of the Passive Voice.

The usage of a to be form of verb ['be' in this case] is necessary while changing the voice of the sentence from Active to Passive.

The question in Active voice is in the imperative form. An imperative sentence is used to express order, request, suggestion, etc. They begin with a principal verb. Here, the imperative sentence in Active voice is an order.

The format in Active voice is: V1 + Object.

Thus, the format in Passive voice will be: Let + Object of the active voice (Subjective case) + be + V3.

For example:

Start the match. (Active)

Let the match be started. (Passive)

The options except (a) dont follow the correct grammatical format of the Passive Voice.

Therefore, the correct answer is: option (a).

questions.q_en:
Select the most appropriate option to substitute the bracketed segment in the given sentence. If there is no need to substitute it, select "no substitution required'.

If the dog (is allow complete freedom), it can assume that any toy is acceptable for play.
questions.solution_en:
The helping verb 'is' should be followed by either past participle (V3) or present participle (V4). Also, the dog is what the action of being allowed complete freedom is subjected at. So, the passive voice construct 'is + allowed' is apt in this case.

The correct sentence is: If the dog is allowed complete freedom, it can assume that any toy is acceptable for play.

Hence, option (a) is the answer.

Note: Active and Passive Voice: When the person doing the action is the subject, the sentence is said to be in active form/voice. When the subject is what the action is directed at, then the sentence is said to be in passive form/voice. For example: Active Voice: Rita and her friends performed a skit. Here 'Rita and her friends' (subject) perform the action. Passive Voice: A skit was performed by Rita and her friends. Here 'skit' is the subject (at which the action is directed).

Select the option that expresses the given sentence in the positive degree of comparison.

This is the easiest math problem I've ever solved.
options_en: This math problem is very easy.
This math problem is easier than others.
This math problem is the easiest of all.
This math problem is not the most difficult.
questions.solution_en:
The original sentence is in the superlative degree, indicating that this math problem is the easiest of all. The correct answer expresses the positive degree by stating that this math problem is very easy without making any comparative or superlative comparisons.

Hence, option (a) is the correct answer.

Option (b) is in comparative degree.

Options (c) and (d) are in superlative degrees.

Note:

Adjectives: Words which are used with a noun/pronoun to describe or point out, the person, animal, place, or thing which the noun names, or to tell the number or quantity, are called Adjectives.

· The Positive Degree is used to denote the mere existence of some quality of what we speak about. It is used when no comparison is made.

· The Comparative degree denotes a higher degree of quality than the positive and is used when two things are compared.

· The Superlative degree indicates the highest degree of quality and is used when more than two things (or sets of things) are compared.

Option (b): "Hesitant" means tentative or unsure. "Innovative" means featuring new methods; advanced and original. These are not synonyms.

Option (c): "Brilliant" means exceptionally clever or talented. "Unique" means being the only one of its kind. They do not mean the same thing.

Option (d): "Perspective" means a particular attitude towards or way of regarding something; a point of view. "Current" means happening or being used or done now. These are not synonyms.

Hence, option (a) is the correct answer.

questions.q_en:
Parts of a sentence are given below in jumbled order. Arrange the parts in the correct order to form a meaningful sentence.

(a) a supportive and non-judgmental environment,

(b) encouraging exploration of diverse interests, providing

(c) and allowing freedom for experimentation

(d) are highly beneficial approaches

(e) to foster creativity in children,
questions.solution_en:
(e) To foster creativity in children, - This introductory infinitive phrase states the purpose or goal of the actions described in the rest of the sentence. It sets the stage.

(b) encouraging exploration of diverse interests, providing - This gerund phrase is the first part of a compound subject, detailing an approach to achieve the goal stated in (e). So far: "To foster creativity in children, encouraging exploration of diverse interests,"

(a) a supportive and non-judgmental environment, - This is the second gerund phrase in the compound subject, parallel to (b), listing another beneficial approach. Now: "...encouraging exploration of diverse interests, providing a supportive and non-judgmental environment,"

(c) and allowing freedom for experimentation - This is the third gerund phrase, connected by "and," completing the list of approaches that form the compound subject. "...providing a supportive and non-judgmental environment, and allowing freedom for experimentation"

(d) are highly beneficial approaches - This is the predicate of the sentence. The verb "are" agrees with the plural compound subject (encouraging, providing, allowing), and "highly beneficial approaches" describes what these actions constitute.

Final sentence: "To foster creativity in children, encouraging exploration of diverse interests, providing a supportive and non-judgmental environment, and allowing freedom for experimentation are highly beneficial approaches."

Hence, option (b) is the answer.

questions.q_en:
Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. If there is no need to substitute it, select 'No substitution'.

The reason for the unexpected project delay is because the main supplier failed to deliver the crucial components on the agreed-upon date, causing a major logistical bottleneck.
options_en: is due to the main supplier
is on account of the main supplier
questions.solution_en:
The phrase "The reason... is because" is a common redundancy in English. The word "reason" implies causality, as does the word "because." Using them together is grammatically superfluous. The correct construction is "The reason is that..." where "that" introduces a noun clause explaining the reason.

Option a) is that the main supplier correctly replaces "because" with "that," eliminating the redundancy and forming a grammatically sound sentence.

Option b) is due to the main supplier is also problematic. "Due to" should typically modify a noun, not follow a linking verb like "is" in this structure. For example, "The delay was due to the supplier's failure."

Option c) is on account of the main supplier is grammatically possible but wordy and less direct than "is that...". Also, it would need to be followed by the -ing form of verb "failing".

So, the correct sentence is: The reason for the unexpected project delay is that the main supplier failed to deliver the crucial components on the agreed-upon date, causing a major logistical bottleneck.

Hence, the most appropriate choice is a) is that the main supplier.

questions.q_en:
Select the option that expresses the given sentence in indirect speech.

David said to me, "I was reading a book when you called me yesterday."
options_en: David told me that he had been reading a book when I called him the previous day.
David told me that he was reading a book when I called him the previous day.
David told me that he was reading a book when I had called him yesterday.
David told me that he had been reading a book when I had called him the previous day.
questions.solution_en:
Option (b) is the correct answer.

If the sentence is in Simple Past, the form of tense doesn't change when it is used in the time clause.

One way of identifying the time clause is that the Time clause always begins with the following: When, whenever, while, as, since, after, before, until, as soon as

For example:

Ayush said to me, "When I saw him, he was working." (Direct Speech)

Ayush told me that when he saw him, he was working. (Indirect Speech)

The following things in the sentence should change when changed from Direct speech to Indirect Speech:

· The reporting verb 'said to' is changed into 'told'.

· The pronouns 'I' into 'he', 'you' into 'I', and 'me' into 'him' are changed.

· 'Yesterday' is changed into 'the previous day'.

Therefore, the correct answer is option (b): David told me that he was reading a book when I called him the previous day.
